*Within-50-Entity Majority Text Generation Headroom Rule (WME): On becoming effective, this rule applies to "entities" and "units of content" associated with text-generation systems capable of human-level text generation. An "entity" is a corporation, individual, or their successor. A "unit of content" is a word, phrase, sentence, paragraph, or document.
An entity owns "units of content" when those units are associated with a commercial general-purpose text-generation system i. which it trains, uses, or has others make material use of to earn monetary assets; ii. to which it owns a direct, variable interest, or iii. that has been identified in an ongoing majority vote for such an entity.”
An entity’s “primary interest” is the set of all units of content identified in an ongoing majority vote to which that entity’s interests are most significant under the rules; all else are "subsidiary interests."
A "WME-covered entity" is an entity whose primary interests, including WME-covered entities and WME-affected entities, own less than 50 of the units of content associated with its primary interests on a pro-rated basis adjusted for the proportion of devices used by each subsidiary interest.
A "WME-affected entity" is an entity whose primary interests are WME-covered by an interest in a WME-covered entity. A WME-covered entity owning >51% of interests in a unit of content associated with its primary interest must relegate all subsidiary interests of that entity by classification such that all those subsidiary interests are counted within their classification for WME-covered purposes. This is recursive.
An "expected vote" for 50+1 control of a corporation's interests with an agency requires an affirmative vote by 50+1 control forfeiture, disqualification, or transfer to another entity of 50+1 votes, excluding preferred stock votes, within 30 days of reporting of corporate interests to an agency. The requirement must be included in either bylaws or charter and must be approved by required 50+1 interest voters known to have voting rights on the entity's board of directors within 30 days of unanimous board approval of the requirement for transfers and elections. Within 90 days, the company must establish a voting right trust or incentive plan for all voting stock to be distributed for any loss of 50+1 control without a prior election or transfer.
If applicable, preferential status for transfers must be extended to voting preferential voting rights for shares in the future under a voting rights trust. If not applicable, the contractual right must required to allow voting rights for shares purchased through transfers on an irrevocable or defeasible basis with no resort to court in event of forfeiture not within a specified time frame.
Such rule must be accorded to corporations with primary interest determinations either directly or by virtue of holding WME-affected units of content. An entity that holds or holds, directly or indirectly under this rule, less than 51% of an entity which is not WME-covered within 30 days of becoming effective is immediately disqualified. If the initial three-month period elapses, a 60-day extension is automatically applied and the entity is disqualified at the end of the extension period. This disqualification is final and not appealable. This rule must take effect prior to the end of the current financial quarter and may not be amended in future unless the initial effective date is changed by the board of directors, in which case it becomes immediately effective. If passed by board vote, the half-life formula for the expected vote will become the majority rule.
